```{r, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
options(width = 750)
library(orthologr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = "#>", collapse = TRUE, error = FALSE, tidy = FALSE)
```

Version 0.5.0 returns other numbers than 0.4.3 for part of the gene pairs, and in some cases other orthologs.
This article says what changed by default and by how much, how to get the results of 0.4.3 back, and what is
new. The complete list of changes is in `NEWS.md`.

## In one line: the results of 0.4.3

```{r, eval = FALSE}
old <- orthologr_legacy_options()   # the settings of 0.4.3, for this session
# ... dNdS(), divergence_stratigraphy(), ...
options(old)                        # back to the defaults of 0.5.0
```

`options(orthologr.legacy = TRUE)` has the same effect (for instance in an `.Rprofile`). The settings are:

```{r}
str(orthologr_legacy_options(set = FALSE))
```

With them, `dNdS()` returns the tables of 0.4.3 for the 20-gene and the 1,000-gene example of the package
(Comeron and YN; same rows, same order, every column identical). The test suite compares the 20-gene result
with tables stored from 0.4.3 on every run. Two things are arguments, not options: T-Coffee ran with
`-mode accurate` in 0.4.3 (`aa_aln_params = "-mode accurate"` restores it), and `aa_aln_params` was ignored for
every alignment program. The settings apply to `engine = "orthologr"` (the default) only: the COAL engine
(`engine = "coal"`, `dNdS_coal()`, `dNdS_clusters()`) aligns the proteins itself and cannot reproduce the
alignments of 0.4.3, so with these settings it warns (class `orthologr_warning_legacy_engine`) and its numbers
differ from those of 0.4.3 (20-gene example: 10 of 20 pairs differ, largest difference in dN/dS 0.147, r = 0.984).

Whether a result was computed with these settings can be read from the result itself:
`attr(result, "orthologr_run")$options`.

## What changed by default, and by how much

| Change | Restored by |
|---|---|
| Best hits are chosen by bit score (was: e-value, then alignment length) | `options(orthologr.best_hit_rule = "evalue")` or `best_hit_rule = "evalue"` |
| Pairwise protein alignments: BLOSUM62, full length, stop codon not aligned | `options(orthologr.legacy_pairwise_aln = TRUE)` |
| Comeron's method returns `NA` for a saturated dN or dS | `options(orthologr.legacy_comeron_saturation = TRUE)` |
| KaKs_Calculator methods return `dN = 0` (was `NA`) for a pair without nonsynonymous change, and dN = dS = 0 for identical sequences | `options(orthologr.legacy_kaks_zero_dn = TRUE)` |
| KaKs_Calculator methods return `NA` (status `"saturated"`) where KaKs_Calculator prints a capped value (e.g. dS = 99), and `NA` with status `"failed"` where it prints `nan` | `options(orthologr.legacy_kaks_saturation = TRUE)` |
| dN/dS tables end with the column `status` | `options(orthologr.status_column = FALSE)` |
| A pairwise protein alignment of more than 5e8 cells (about 1.5 GB) is not computed; the pair is `"failed"` | `options(orthologr.max_aln_cells = Inf)` |
| T-Coffee runs in its default mode | `aa_aln_params = "-mode accurate"` |

### Best hits by bit score

DIAMOND and BLAST report an e-value of 0 for every strong hit of a long protein. Under the rule of 0.4.3
(smallest e-value, then longest alignment) the alignment length then decided, and a paralog with a longer but
worse alignment could win over the ortholog. The best hit is now the hit with the highest bit score (then
smallest e-value, longest alignment, highest identity, alphabetically first subject).

| DIAMOND, reciprocal best hits | rule of 0.4.3 | bit score |
|---|---|---|
| human / mouse (19,746 x 21,584 genes): pairs | 16,458 | 16,827 |
| ... pairs that contradict the orthologs of Ensembl Compara | 330 (2.0 %) | 68 (0.4 %) |
| ... Compara one-to-one orthologs found | 93.0 % | 96.8 % |
| 1,000-gene example of the package: pairs | 972 | 983 (970 in common) |

3.2 % of the human / mouse best hits change; on the 1,000-gene example 12 of 986 best hits.

### Pairwise protein alignments

`dNdS()` aligns the two proteins of a gene pair with `pwalign::pairwiseAlignment(type = "global")`. Up to 0.4.3
no substitution matrix was used (every mismatch cost the same), the overhanging ends of the longer protein were
cut off, and the stop codon was aligned and scored. Now the alignment is scored with BLOSUM62
(`aa_sub_matrix`), written full length, and made without the stop codon.

1,000-gene example (984 reciprocal best hits under the old best-hit rule), 0.4.3 against the new alignments:

| | Comeron (default) | YN (KaKs_Calculator) |
|---|---|---|
| pairs with unchanged dN and dS | 66 % (651 of 984) | 71 % (699 of 984) |
| Pearson r of dN, old vs new | 0.971 | 0.967 |
| Pearson r of dS, old vs new | 0.940 | 0.997 (0.985 without two nearly saturated pairs) |
| Pearson r of dN/dS, old vs new | 0.988 | 0.984 |
| largest change of dN / dS / dN/dS | 0.19 / 0.41 / 0.31 | 0.19 / 0.48 / 0.44 |
| pairs whose dN/dS changes by more than 0.01 | 22 % | 20 % |

About a third of the gene pairs get other values. For most the change is small (median change of dN 0.002, of
dS 0.004 to 0.005 among the changed pairs); for single pairs it is large, and rankings or thresholds on dN/dS
(`filter_dNdS()`, divergence strata) can move.

### Saturation in Comeron's method

When two sequences differ at more sites of a class than the model can correct for, the logarithm of the
correction has no value. 0.4.3 replaced it by 0 and returned a finite, too small dN or dS (one synonymous
substitution in three codons gave dS = 0). Such a value, and dN/dS, is now `NA` and the pair has status
`"saturated"`. All other values are unchanged.

| gene pairs (same codon alignments in both modes) | dS: value -> `NA` | dN: value -> `NA` | dN/dS: value -> `NA` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000-gene example, default: 995 pairs | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| ... with `best_hit_rule = "evalue"`: 984 pairs | 0 | 3 | 0 |
| human / mouse, 1,500 pairs (gene families, long genes, random pairs) | 1 | 17 | 5 (1,487 -> 1,482 with a value) |

Very short alignments are affected more often (30 codons: several percent of random pairs lose dN).

### dN = 0 with the KaKs_Calculator methods

KaKs_Calculator prints `NA` for every Ka below 1e-6 and still prints `Ka/Ks = 0`. orthologr returned
`dN = NA`, `dNdS = 0`, and `filter_dNdS()` / `divergence_stratigraphy()` then left out exactly the most conserved
genes. Now `dN = 0`. 1,000-gene example, YN: 11 of 995 pairs change from `dN = NA` to `dN = 0` (their `dNdS` was
and is 0); `filter_dNdS()` kept 984 of the 995 pairs and now keeps all 995.

In the same way identical sequences (KaKs_Calculator: `NA NA NA`) now have dN = dS = 0 (status `"dS_zero"`, as
with the COAL engine) instead of three `NA` and the status `"saturated"`, and a pair with nonsynonymous
differences only has dS = 0. E. coli K-12 / O157, YN: 230 of 3,663 pairs; a file compared with itself is no
longer reported as "saturated - the species are probably too distant".

### Saturated estimates of the KaKs_Calculator methods

Where the correction for multiple substitutions is not defined, KaKs_Calculator prints a capped number instead of
`NA`: dS = 99, JC69's distance at its cap (0.75 log of the number of sites; dS of about 2.5 - 6) for YN and MYN,
or 0 substitutions for a class of sites in the LWL family. orthologr returned these as estimates (status
`"ok"`). Now they are `NA` with the status `"saturated"`, as with the COAL engine.
S. cerevisiae / C. glabrata, YN: 3,559 of 4,164 pairs (172 of them with dS = 99, whose dN/dS of about 0.003 put
them into the most conserved divergence stratum); E. coli K-12 / O157: 21 of 3,663; 1,000-gene example: 1 of 995.
Where KaKs_Calculator prints `nan` (its estimate failed; MYN, S. cerevisiae / C. glabrata: 50 of 4,164 pairs) the
pair is `NA` with the status `"failed"` and the reason in `attr(result, "failed_pairs")` (was `NaN` and
`"saturated"`). KaKs_Calculator does not report whether the YN / MYN iteration converged; such pairs keep the
values of its last round and the status `"ok"` (3 % of the yeast YN estimates).
`options(orthologr.legacy_kaks_saturation = TRUE)` returns the printed numbers.

### Not a default change: gene pairs with dS = 0

`filter_dNdS()` and `divergence_stratigraphy()` leave gene pairs with dS = 0 out, as every released version
did - but they now say so: a message gives the number of pairs left out per reason, and
`divergence_left_out()` returns them. `dS_zero = "keep"` keeps them with `dNdS = NA`.

## New in the result: status, summary and the record of the run

```{r, eval = FALSE}
res <- dNdS(query_file   = system.file("seqs/ortho_thal_cds.fasta", package = "orthologr"),
            subject_file = system.file("seqs/ortho_lyra_cds.fasta", package = "orthologr"))
#> dNdS(): reciprocal best hits of 'ortho_thal_cds.fasta' against 'ortho_lyra_cds.fasta' (diamond, ...
#> dNdS(): 20 gene pairs - 20 with dN/dS. Median dS: 0.154.

table(res$status)
#> ok
#> 20
```

* **`status`** is the last column of every dN/dS table: `"ok"`, `"dS_zero"` (dS is 0, no ratio),
  `"saturated"` (dN or dS not estimable), `"no_data"` (no codons to compare) or `"failed"` (a program failed
  for the pair; reason in `attr(res, "failed_pairs")`). Code that addresses columns by position from the end,
  or binds tables of 0.4.3 and 0.5.0, should select columns by name or set
  `options(orthologr.status_column = FALSE)`.
* **The summary** at the end of a run counts the gene pairs by status and gives the median dS. When more than a
  fifth of the pairs is saturated or the median dS is above 1.5 it says that the species are probably too
  distant for pairwise dN/dS. *S. cerevisiae* against *C. glabrata*: 3,012 of 4,164 pairs (72 %) have no dS,
  and the median dS of the others is 1.9 - 0.4.3 and earlier development versions returned this table without
  a word.
* **`attr(res, "orthologr_run")`** records the package version, the arguments, every `orthologr.*` option, the
  engine, the versions of the programs, the date, size and MD5 checksum of the input files and the counts by
  status. Attributes do not survive most table operations or `write.table()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
write_dNdS(res, "thal_lyra_dnds.tsv")     # the table, and thal_lyra_dnds.tsv.run.json next to it
res <- read_dNdS("thal_lyra_dnds.tsv")    # table and attributes
attr(res, "orthologr_run")$tools
```

Messages: `dNdS()` writes nothing to `stdout` any more (the citation was printed there). With `quiet = TRUE`,
the default, a run gives one line at the start and the summary (before: 31 messages for the 20-gene example);
`quiet = FALSE` adds the parameters, the messages of the search program and a progress line about every tenth
of the gene pairs. The citation note is shown once per session.

## Behaviour that changed and has no switch

* One gene pair can no longer end a run: a pair whose alignment or estimation fails is a row of `NA` values
  with status `"failed"`.
* A missing program and unsupported argument values are errors before the search starts.
* Parameter strings (`aa_aln_params`, `aligner_params`, `diamond_params`, `blast_params`, ...) are lists of
  arguments, not shell text; see `?orthologr_options`.
* Sequence IDs come back exactly as they are in the input files (IDs with `-`, `|`, digits only, or more than
  15 characters lost rows or were changed).
* Li's method returns numbers (it returned text, and took values such as `9.95e-05` for the saturation marker).
* Intermediate files live in a folder of the call inside `tempdir()`; nothing is written into the working
  directory unasked.
* `ggplot2`, `scales`, `ape`, `rtracklayer`, `benchmarkme`, `tidyr`, `biomartr` and `metablastr` are in
  Suggests: install them when a function asks for them.

## New functions

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `orthogroups()`, `write_orthogroups()` | groups of orthologs of 2 to N species with DIAMOND (replaces the OrthoFinder interface) |
| `dNdS_orthogroups()` | dN/dS for the gene pairs within orthogroups, with a summary per group |
| `divergence_left_out()` | the gene pairs that are not in a divergence map, and why |
| `write_dNdS()`, `read_dNdS()` | a dN/dS table with the record of its run |
| `orthologr_legacy_options()` | the settings of 0.4.3 |
| `?orthologr_options` | every option and environment variable |

New arguments: `best_hit_rule`, `aa_sub_matrix`, `dS_zero`.

## The COAL engine (optional)

With the R package `coalr` installed, `dNdS(engine = "coal")` (= `dNdS_coal()`) hands all gene pairs to
[COAL](https://github.com/Plumat-COAL/COAL) in one call: protein alignment, codon alignment and estimation in
memory, on `comp_cores` threads, without Perl or KaKs_Calculator. The table has the columns of `dNdS()`,
including `status`; COAL's own table (standard errors, sites, notes) is `attr(result, "coal")`. On the
1,000-gene example it takes about 6 s on one core (default engine: 50 s). `dNdS_clusters()` computes dN/dS
within DIAMOND DeepClust clusters, and `dNdS_orthogroups(engine = "coal")` within orthogroups;
`codon_aln(tool = "coal")` and `substitutionrate(kaks_tool = "coal")` replace single steps. The values agree
with the default engine for the same codon alignment; where a protein alignment has several equally good
solutions the two aligners can place a gap differently, which changes the values of about a third of the gene
pairs of the 1,000-gene example slightly. Nothing changes for calls that do not ask for COAL.

## Soft-deprecated

* `orthofinder2()` warns on every call (it never worked beyond starting the program): use `orthogroups()`.
* `cdd.path` and `ortho_path` of `dNdS()` (never used) give a warning when set.
* `ortho_detection = "Orthofinder2"`, `"PO"` and `"DELTA"` are errors that name the alternatives.

## Speed

Default `dNdS()` on the 1,000-gene example (one core, same machine): 744 s with 0.4.3 and 50 s with 0.5.0
(27 s with two cores); with the legacy settings 0.5.0 takes as long as 0.4.3, because the old alignment
scoring is the slow part.
